result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | Edgecase description: >- A high-performance graph data structure with optional direction and weights. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | Edgecase description: >- A high-performance graph data structure with optional direction and weights. title: "[Graph]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- A high-performance graph data structure with optional direction and weights. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} A high-performance graph data structure with optional direction and weights. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L315-L73671){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature Graph( directed=False, weighted=False, nodes_df=None, edges_df=None, graph_name=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The `Graph` class provides a Python interface to a Rust-based graph implementation, offering both performance and ease of use. Nodes are identified by 64-bit unsigned integers (u64 IDs) and can optionally have string labels for human-readable access. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [directed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether the graph should be directed. If `True`, edges have direction from source to target. If `False`, edges are bidirectional. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether edges can have weights. If `True`, edge weights are stored and considered in algorithms. If `False`, all edges are treated equally. [nodes_df]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[pl.DataFrame]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional Polars DataFrame to initialize nodes. Should contain at minimum an `id` column with node identifiers. The values in the `id` column are used as node *labels* (not internal node IDs, which are auto-managed). Additional columns are treated as node attributes. [edges_df]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[pl.DataFrame]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional Polars DataFrame to initialize edges. Should contain at minimum `from` and `to` columns with node identifiers that reference the `id` values from `nodes_df`. Additional columns are treated as edge attributes (including optional `weight` column). [graph_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional name for the graph (stored as a graph attribute). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The simplest way to build a graph is to chain `add_node()` and `add_edge()` calls, since both return `self`. Printing the graph shows a summary of its structure: ::: {#1b9165db .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="Alice") .add_node(label="Bob") .add_edge(source="Alice", target="Bob") ) graph ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` Number of nodes : 2 Number of edges : 1 Directed : False Density : 1.00 Average degree (min, max) : 1.00 (1, 1) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : True Bipartite : True ``` ::: ::: A graph can also be built from existing tabular data by passing Polars DataFrames. The `id` column in `nodes_df` becomes each node's label, and `from`/`to` in `edges_df` reference those same labels: ::: {#9fece546 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl nodes_df = pl.DataFrame({ "id": ["A", "B", "C"], "type": ["person", "person", "person"], "value": [10, 20, 15] }) edges_df = pl.DataFrame({ "from": ["A", "B"], "to": ["B", "C"], "weight": [1.5, 2.0], "relation": ["friend", "colleague"] }) graph = ec.Graph(nodes_df=nodes_df, edges_df=edges_df, directed=True, weighted=True) graph ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` Number of nodes : 3 Number of edges : 2 Directed : True Density : 0.33 Average degree (min, max) : 1.33 (1, 2) Strongly connected : False Weakly connected : True Number of strongly connected components : 3 Number of weakly connected components : 1 ``` ::: ::: Setting `directed=True` and `weighted=True` produces a graph suited to modeling flows or distances, where each edge has both a direction and a numeric cost: ::: {#cdfc27f8 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True) .add_node(label="Alice") .add_node(label="Bob") .add_edge(source="Alice", target="Bob", weight=0.8) ) graph ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` Number of nodes : 2 Number of edges : 1 Directed : True Density : 0.50 Average degree (min, max) : 1.00 (1, 1) Strongly connected : False Weakly connected : True Number of strongly connected components : 2 Number of weakly connected components : 1 ``` ::: :::
